findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple chemical sanitizers failing to meet sanitizing concentrations for food contact surfaces: 
1) The dish machine was observed to be failing to dispense sanitizer (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- the sanitizer bottle was replaced, and observed to be meeting required concentration for the sanitization of food contact surfaces. 
2) The bar triple sink was observed at 10 ppm Cl. CORRECTED- the sanitizer compartment was remade to 150 ppm Cl.
Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration recommended by the manufacturers label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee turned off the faucets with their bare hands after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment:
Observed the following did not have scoops with handles:

(1) The parmesan cheese in the salad prep cooler. 

(2) The sugar container in the server station. 

The cheese and sugar scoops were removed from the containers during the inspection and replaced with scoops with handles. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods always have handles to prevent bare hand contact with the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following posed the risk of contamination:

(1) Several plastic container tops with large cracks in the pizza prep cooler.

(2) A rubber spatula with several cracks by the salad prep cooler. 

The container tops and rubber spatula were discarded during the inspection. The PIC was educated that damaged equipment must be discarded if they pose a risk of contamination. Ensure that food is always protected from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket in the kitchen when the inspectors arrived. During the inspection a sanitizer bucket was made testing at 400 ppm (quat). Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.

(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.comment: Observed the mop sink needs to be re-caulked to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the mop sink is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection.

findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces are in need of cleaning: (1) Food debris inside buckets holding clean utensils by the kitchen entrance; (2) Dusty solid silver shelves above prep tables; (3) Soiled silver and green shelves holding clean dishes by the dish machine area; and (4) Dusty fan by the mop sink. findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS ROUTINE INSPECTION(S).

Inspector observed several remaining flies in warewashing area of the kitchen where flies were observed previously. The number of flies observed is significantly less than previously observed. However, the number of flies still constitutes a violation and requires additional corrective actions. Discussed with operator the need to have pest control do more to eliminate the flies from the facility. No follow-up required. Continue working toward resolution. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Several nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment are observed to be moderately soiled including but not limited to the undersides of shelving and within coolers. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Mold growth within cold-holding units remains a problem at the facility. Inspector opened the drawers and cabinet doors of the far south prep cooler along the east wall of the kitchen and observed mold and other residue still present as well as standing water. Cold holding units must be cleaned and then sanitized to prevent cross-contamination of foods stored within. Further, seals on virtually cold-holding doors have mold present. These seals must be cleaned/replaced. Operator states that they are being replaced. Seals must remain clean in the meantime while food is being stored in these coolers. Surfaces underneath counters and coolers and the east wall of the kitchen remain soiled. Ensure that these surfaces are clean to sight and touch and have all been sanitized.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Inspector observed flies continuing to be present although in significantly decreased numbers from the inspection on 07/18/2023. Surfaces in the kitchen remain unclean and pose a significant hazard of contaminating food should they remain in this condition. Cleaning in the ware washing area of the facility remains excellent. Ensure that the remainder of the kitchen is cleaned in a similar fashion.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11:  The present daytime manager should be communicating with other managers to determine areas of concerns related to cleaning. The entire facility illustrates a lack of detail cleaning. Corners, crevices, and undersides of counters/equipment/shelving is observed with an accumulation of molds, soil, and debris. Management stated that they have a daily checklist to complete and it appears the checklist is either not inclusive of cleaning or that step is being missed. Facility would benefit from meeting of management to determine how best to handle situations related to missed cleaning activities. Facility will be receiving a number of follow-ups to monitor the cleaning, educating of staff, and discussion of routine checks conducted by management. 
Facility will be checked on 7/19 to observe cleaning of the dish room.
Facility will be checked on  7/24 to check on cleaning condition of facility.
Facility will be checked on 7/31 to check on education of staff - show proof (attendance log) of staff meeting related to cleaning strategies.
Facility will be checked on 8/31 to check on active managerial monitoring.

 Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11:  Facility is in danger of cross-contaminating food due to present of drain and house flies throughout facility. Flies are observed throughout the dish area and kitchen space. Facility was asked to discard a bag of flour due to the presence of flies within the bag and in-contact with food material. The facility received pest control nearly two weeks prior but will need to clean, service, and use a enzymatic cleaner to treat the floor drains. See that food is kept covered to protect from fly presence but also the mold growth observed within the interior of cold holding units. Soil and molds are not simply limited to interiors, but, at this time, that is the concern for food safety. Clean surfaces to eliminate fly presence and mold accumulation. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The entire facility is potentially a source of cross-contamination due to presence of soil, pests, and molds. The facility was asked to halt service for a few hours to clean the dish area and not have clean dishes present while the activity occurs. Facility manager stated that they are not busy between 2 and 4pm and will be able to clean and not increase potential for cross-contamination during the cleaning of the dish area. Flies are known disease carriers - landing on food and equipment is a potential source of foodborne illness. See that you move through the kitchen in a clock-wise and systematic method cleaning equipment and surfaces. 
 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Facility has several dozen drain flies observed throughout the dish area and kitchen. Additional numbers of house flies are observed throughout the lobby and kitchen. Facility has called for pest control service and needs to supplement with cleaning. Floors, walls, and equipment are observed thickly coated with accumulated soil and filth. The soiled drains, available water, and available food soil provide harborage, water, and food for pests. The facility needs to do more than simply treat for pests. Cleaning and maintenance behaviors of staff should be evaluated. See that pest control increases the frequency of visits, but also see that staff is held accountable for the cleaning tasks.  

PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-603.14: The facility should be using the dish machine and triple sink, in-combination as necessary, to remove soil and debris from equipment without the potential to be re-contaminated due to the surrounding soil. The soil and presence of pests presents an immediate concern for cross-contamination of clean equipment and dishes within the dish room. See that ware washing is halted during the cleaning of the dish area. Facility should focus on cleaning this room and cease dish activity during that time. SCDPH will be returning 7/19 to observe cleaning progress - specifically the floors, walls, and equipment found within the dish room. 

 (A) EQUIPMENT shall be effectively washed to remove or completely loosen soils. (B) Washing procedures selected shall be based on type and purpose of EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The facility illustrates a lack of detail cleaning as every counter, shelf, and cooler is observed soiled with accumulated food debris. The interior of the preparation cooler is specifically observed to hold an egregious amount of ponding water and food. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-202.11: There are four floor drains in the dish area that are observed encrusted with food debris. The drains are providing a source of food and harborage and should be cleaned and treated. 
(A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
The facility has been cited for several priority/priority foundation violations and repeat violations from previous inspections. Due to the severity of these violations and the potential hazards associated with continuation of these violations, inspector will return in 30-days to evaluate progress towards compliance with 2017 FDA Food Code requirements. Ensure that all staff are aware of the violations observed today and the corrective actions that must be taken to correct the violations in question. Inspector will return on Wednesday 05/17/2023 for follow-up on all priority/priority foundation violations.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand sink at the front server station has a soap dispenser which was empty during the inspection. Hand sinks must be stocked with soap at all times to facilitate hand washing. Ensure that staff are aware of this requirement and know where hand soap is located to replenish it as necessary. Ensure that hand sinks are stocked with soap at all times. A follow-up is issued for 10-days to ensure compliance with this requirement. Inspector will return on 04/27/2023.

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
During the inspection, inspector observed a prep cooler with a large amount of mold growth on the inside of the cooler. The mold and lime scale has covered all surfaces inside the cooler. The cooler has pools of water on all lower surfaces with visible white, green and black mold growth. Black mold growth is observed on the upper surface and dripping down towards the lower edges of baffles, potentially dripping onto foods below it. Foods within the cooler were uncovered. All foods were removed from the cooler immediately. Water must removed from the cooler and the all surfaces within the cooler must be cleaned and sanitized and inspector must provide approval before foods may be stored in the cooler again. Inspector will return in three days to follow-up on the status of the cooler unless contacted earlier by operator. Foods must be protected from contamination at all times. Ensure that foods are stored in a manner that prevent ANY cross-contamination at ANY time. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 09/13/2022.

At the rear of the facility, inspector observed a large dough hook used to prepare fresh dough in the facility stored, dirty, directly on a wire rack for continued use. The dough hook was potentially contaminated immediately upon placing it on the dirty, unsanitized wire rack. The hook must be cleaned, sanitized and stored in a manner that prevents contamination. As long as the hook remains in use for only the single purpose of preparing raw dough, cleaning does not need to occur between use but it may only be stored on cleaned and sanitized surfaces between uses.

Also on a wire rack at the rear of the facility was an in-use cutting board placed underneath the dirty, unsanitized wire rack directly on the external, potentially contaminated, containers of flour. The cutting board was soiled with raw dough. The cutting board must be cleaned, sanitized and stored in a manner that prevents contamination as long as it remains used for the same purpose. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces being stored between uses are stored ONLY on cleaned/sanitized surfaces and remain protected from any form of contamination.

Inspector will return on Thursday 04/20/2023 to evaluate corrective actions.

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 09/13/2022. 

There are approximately ten flies at the rear of the facility near and within the hampers containing wet wiping cloths and soiled mop heads. Aramark collects these items for laundering once per week. This may not be suficient to prevent harborage of pests within these items. Ensure that the premise is inspected for pests and insects, especially flies, often and that harborage conditions such as sacks of wet soiled linens are eliminated from the facility to prevent worsening pest/insect problems. Contact third party pest control if store efforts to remove them are unsuccessful. Improve cleaning practices to further eliminate harborage conditions. 

Inspector will return on 04/27/2023 to evaluate progress towards eliminating insects from the facility.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several wet wiping cloths sitting on countertops throughout the course of the inspection today. Wet wiping cloths may ONLY be stored in sanitizer solution between uses unless placed in laundry. Enusre that wet wiping cloths are stored properly between uses. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
In-use knives and spatulas along both sides of the kitchen were observed stored underneath carboard boxes, a glove box, and a soiled plastic container. In-use utensils must be stored on properly cleaned and sanitized surfaces between uses. Food contact surfaces of utenils must be protected from contamination and never stored in contact with unclean, unsanitized surfaces. Ensure that staff are aware of how to properly store utensils between uses. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Wiping cloths and mop heads are stored in cloth hampers at the rear of the facility. These items are laundered by Aramark weekly. Wet wiping cloths must be laundered daily. Mop cloths must be laundered between operations. Ensure that these items are laundered as often as required to prevent contamination and pests.

4-802.11: (A) LINENS not in direct contact with FOOD shall be laundered between operations if soiled. (B) Cloth gloves shall be laundered before being used with different raw animal FOOD. (C) LINENS and cloth napkins shall be laundered between customers, when being used as food holding liner. (D) Wet wiping cloths shall be laundered daily. (E) Dry wiping cloths shall be laundered as necessary to prevent contamination of FOOD and UTENSILS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM INSPECTION DATED 09/13/2022.

All non-food-contact surfaces of equipment must be cleaned more frequently. Non-food-contact surfaces throughout the facility are observed to have an accumulation of residue and debris. Ensure that cleaning throughout the facility occurs and that non-food-contat surfaces of equipment are included in the cleaning regimen. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Chipped paint at the corner of the wall to the left while EXITING the bar must be repainted/repaired. Surfaces in food preparation/service areas must be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that all surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable and that all surfaces subject to food/moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The facility is in need of immediate, in-depth cleaning throughout. Areas underneath and behind equipment and shelving are of particular concern. Inspector observed refuse, residue and debris throughout the facility that must be cleaned and removed. Ensure that cleaning is happening often enought to prevent the accumulation of debris, especially in hard-to-reach areas.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Inspector observed personal cell phones, phone chargers, sunglass and other items. Personal items are NOT to be stored in food preparation areas of the facility. Employees must have a designated area for personal items that protects food from contamination during preparation. Ensure that all employees are aware of where personal items may be stored and that cell phones are not in-use/being charged in food service areas. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed facility to not have a Norovirus illness clean-up policy (with bleach to perform procedure) and/or a bodily fluid clean-up kit that kills for Norovirus. Facility utilizes EcoLab. A kit can be purchased through EcoLab. A policy was provided during the inspection. Facility has ability to perform procedure (bleach for food-contact surfaces noted). COS. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
REPEAT 1) From inspection conducted on 3/4/22:  Soda nozzle at the pepsi machine observed to have mold. Discussed with staff at facility. Ensure nozzles are removed and washed, rinsed, sanitized daily. Ensure the dispenser is cleaned as well when nozzles are being cleaned.

2). All shelving by dish area was observed to contain dust and debris build-up.  Discussed with staff about cleaning shelving regularly.  Ensure shelving is regularly cleaned to prevent contamination of clean dishes.

3). Container containing pizza serving utensils was observed to contain food debris.  Container shall be free of dust and food debris to prevent contamination of food-contact surfaces.  Ensure container is cleaned regularly.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed drain flies in two areas:
1. Under the soda machine area near the server station (front). Open the bottom cabinet and one will see drain flies below where the soda lines are present.
2. The bar 3 compartment sink/dump sinks have drain flies present.

Ensure both areas are eradicated of pests. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 9/23/22.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Clean wet cups were observed to be stacked on top of one another before drying.  Clean equipment shall be stored in a way air drying is obtained.  Ensure cups are dry before stacking to prevent contamination.

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Temperature measuring device was not available to measure water temperature in dish machine.  Sanitizer is not used in dish machine, sanitization is obtained by water temperature.  Discussed with PIC on ways to obtain a measuring device to regularly check temperature.  Ensure device is obtained by follow-up date.

4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Pizza racks (2x) were observed to contain food debris.  Discussed with staff the frequency of cleaning pizza racks to prevent food debris build-up.  Ensure racks are cleaned frequently. The metal cart by the stove area has food splash and debris. Ensure routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Multiple areas are in need of caulking to obtain a smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
1). Sinks in bathrooms were observed to need caulk.
2). 3-part sink along the top of the sink was observed to need re-caulked.
3). Front hand washing sink was observed to need re-caulked (on the interior edges of the sink).
Ensure sinks are caulked so that sinks are flush with the wall.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Many employees are not in compliance with the food handler law.  All food handlers are required to obtain certification within 30 days of employment.  Ensure employees are certified by next routine inspection and certification is kept on file and readily available.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
All CFM’s are required to obtain allergen training within 30 days of employment.  Discussed with PIC who is the only CFM with allergen training.  Ensure remaining CFM’s receive allergen training by next routine inspection. Keep copies with employee files.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 
Soda nozzle at the pepsi machine observed to have mold. Discussed with staff at facility. Ensure nozzles are removed and washed, rinsed, sanitized daily. Ensure the dispenser is cleaned as well when nozzles are being cleaned. COS- nozzles removed for cleaning and dispenser cleaned.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test strips for Chlorine sanitizers currently in use at facility not available. Ensure test strips are on hand for all possible chemical sanitizers in use at restaurant. Text/call inspector when purchased.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Food debris and general food splash observed on walls around pizza prep cooler and on doors of prep/cold holding equipment. Ensure these areas are kept free of debris.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A) See violation #8. Observed improper handwashing by PIC at time of inspection. Provided education. Observed PIC again use bare hands to shut off faucet and a third time lightly rinse off fingertips and shut off faucet with bare hands. 
Ensure proper handwashing is modeled at all times and that proper handwashing technique is used each time hand sink is visited.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (Pf) (O) Employee reporting agreements not provided at time of inspection. Discussed employee reporting with PIC and provided education. Will follow up to ensure forms are signed. 

Note: Facility does utilize a sick log. No reportable illnesses and symptoms reported.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12  (P) Observed improper handwashing at time of inspection. Employee shut off faucet with bare hands. Education provided. 
Ensure all employees are washing hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, using a barrier to shut off faucet.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Chopped tomato and ground sausage is not marked with a use-by date. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed with person in charge. Food was prepared the day prior. Food was relabled at time of inspection.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Ice scoop observed stored in between bottles of mixers at the bar. Cease this practice. Ice scoop should be kept in either its own container or in ice with handle extending out of the ice.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14  (Pf) Test strips for Chlorine sanitizer at bar 3-part sink are not available. Ensure test strips for both sanitizers at facility are purchased.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Food debris build up observed in the pizza prep coolers and in the tall vertical coolers. Ensure these items are kept free of food debris. Will check at next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer buckets to test between 0 and 100 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. These are prepared from the wall mounted dispenser at the three compartment sink. There appeared to be lots of air bubbles in the line for the quaternary ammonium, and once this dispenser was run for a period of time, the air bubbles cleared and unit began dispensing at 400 ppm. Sanitizer buckets were re-made to this concentration. Spray bottles with bleach sanitizer solution in them were testing in excess of 200 ppm. Prepare chlorine sanitizer solution to 200 ppm as indicated by the label on the bleach in the facility. 4-501.114  (P) Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed handles to coolers, freezers and equipment, insides of coolers, and the top inside lid on the salad prep cooler to be soiled with soil and food splash accumulation. Clean and sanitize these non-food contact surfaces regularly to prevent contamination of hands and gloves. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
